newsitem.title: USA: US Rep. Archer says movement made on Medicare cuts.
newsitem.headline: US Rep. Archer says movement made on Medicare cuts.

text.p: House Ways and Means Committee Chairman Bill Archer said Thursday that movement had been made on Medicare savings in budget talks and an agreement could be reached if President Clinton resisted pressure from some Democrats.

"If the president can resist pressure from liberal Democrats who want him to avoid making a Medicare agreement with congressional Republicans, I'm optimistic that a Medicare agreement can be reached and reached quickly," Archer, a Texas Republican, told reporters.
There were a lot of differences that still needed to be ironed out, but there had been movement on Medicare since the budget negotiations started, Archer told reporters.
"The number, and the differences in the number, have narrowed dramatically since the negotiations began," he said, but would not comment on specific figures.
The White House has put $100 billion in Medicare savings over five years on the table in budget negotiations and Republicans are seeking about $20 billion more.
